title: Printable coordinate grid sheet
subject: Mathematics
unit: Summer 2: Statistics; geometry; position and direction
source: Seeded from mathematics/y4 lessons 100, 101, 102 (Printable coordinate grid sheet)
intro: To understand how to read and describe positions using coordinates in the first quadrant

model.title: A point is 4 across and 3 up. Coordinates?

parts.label: Step 2
parts.text: Join in order and back to the start.

questions.q: Point 3 across, 7 up?
What is at (0, 0)?
Point on the x-axis 5 across?
Plot (4, 0), (4, 4), (0, 4): add the origin. What shape?
questions.model: Teacher plots the points: all sides 4, so a square.

questions.q: Triangle (1, 1), (5, 1), (3, 4): what type?
Fourth vertex of square (3, 1), (6, 1), (6, 4)?
Translate (1, 2) 3 right.
Translate (6, 4) 2 down.
Describe (2, 2) to (5, 6).
Write the coordinates of the 6 points on the grid sheet.
Which two points have the same x-coordinate?
Write 3 points on the line from (0, 0) to (5, 5).
Plot and join the 3 shapes on the sheet; name each.
Find the missing vertex of each rectangle on the sheet.
A kite has vertices (3, 6), (5, 4), (3, 0). Find the fourth.
Translate the 3 shapes on the sheet as shown; write the new vertices.
Describe the translation from (1, 5) to (4, 2).
A shape is translated 2 right, 3 up, then 5 left, 1 down. Describe one translation that does the same.
Big question: how can two numbers give a position?
Big question: can you draw a shape from coordinates?
questions.a: Yes: plot each vertex and join them in order.

questions.q: A translation...
Big question: how can a shape move without turning?
questions.a: By a translation: every point slides the same distance and direction.
